glossary.definition: A chunk of text the model reads or generates; billing and context limits are counted in tokens.
glossary.de_analogy: Like rows or bytes processed—your cost and SLA driver.

glossary.definition: Maximum tokens the model can consider in one request (prompt + completion).
glossary.de_analogy: Like a max batch size—overflow means truncate, summarize, or chunk.

glossary.definition: Running a trained model to produce outputs (not training).
glossary.de_analogy: Running a scoring job in prod vs retraining the model.

glossary.definition: Model output that looks plausible but is factually wrong or unsupported.
glossary.de_analogy: Bad join or null handling that still returns a row—never trust without validation.

glossary.definition: Forcing LLM responses into a schema (JSON/Pydantic) instead of free text.
glossary.de_analogy: Contract-first API response types and schema enforcement.

glossary.definition: Python library for data validation and settings using type hints.
glossary.de_analogy: Runtime schema checks like Great Expectations on a single record.

glossary.definition: Library that pairs LLM calls with Pydantic models and retries on validation failure.
glossary.de_analogy: Retry loop around a flaky API until the payload passes JSON schema.

glossary.definition: Gateway that routes requests to many model providers with one API.
glossary.de_analogy: API gateway + provider failover for model endpoints.

glossary.definition: Central entry for models: auth, routing, budgets, logging, fallbacks.
glossary.de_analogy: Kong/Apigee-style layer before downstream services.

glossary.definition: Fixed labeled examples (input → expected output) used to score changes.
glossary.de_analogy: Fixture tables in dbt tests or regression datasets.

glossary.definition: Scripts/CI that run the golden set and report metrics on every change.
glossary.de_analogy: pytest + data diff job in CI.

glossary.definition: Business rule beyond JSON shape (e.g. balances sum to zero).
glossary.de_analogy: Custom SQL tests or domain constraints.

glossary.definition: Time to first token—latency until the model starts streaming output.
glossary.de_analogy: Time-to-first-byte on an API response.

glossary.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant docs, then answer with the model.
glossary.de_analogy: Join to a reference table before computing a metric.

glossary.definition: Vector representation of text used for similarity search.
glossary.de_analogy: Feature vector for fuzzy matching instead of exact keys.

glossary.definition: Framework for agent workflows as graphs with state and checkpoints.
glossary.de_analogy: Airflow DAG with per-run state and human approval nodes.

glossary.definition: Persisted graph state so a run can resume after failure or interrupt.
glossary.de_analogy: Idempotent checkpoint in Spark/Flink or workflow saga state.

glossary.definition: Human-in-the-loop: pause automation for review before continuing.
glossary.de_analogy: Manual approval step in a pipeline.

glossary.definition: System that plans steps and calls tools; not just one LLM prompt.
glossary.de_analogy: Orchestrated micro-jobs with side effects—not a single SQL statement.

glossary.definition: Model Context Protocol—standard way to expose tools and resources to models.
glossary.de_analogy: Internal tool catalog + OpenAPI for agents.

glossary.definition: JSON schema describing parameters an agent tool accepts.
glossary.de_analogy: API request body contract.

glossary.definition: Append-only record of who invoked which tool with what outcome.
glossary.de_analogy: CloudTrail / data access logs for compliance.

glossary.definition: Metric got worse vs baseline on the golden set after a change.
glossary.de_analogy: CI test failure on main metrics.

glossary.definition: Secondary model or provider used when the primary fails or is slow.
glossary.de_analogy: Secondary region or read replica failover.

glossary.definition: How the model picks the next token (temperature, top-p).
glossary.de_analogy: Random seed / tie-break policy—lower temperature = more deterministic.

glossary.definition: Mechanism for the model to weigh which input tokens matter for each output token.
glossary.de_analogy: Weighted join keys—without math depth, just “focus mechanism.”

glossary.definition: Neural architecture using self-attention (stacked blocks) that powers modern LLMs; decoder-only variants predict the next token.
glossary.de_analogy: A parallelizable scoring pipeline over a sequence—cost scales with length and width, not a single SQL lookup.

program_pace.primary_audience: Data, analytics, and platform engineers who already ship pipelines, tests, and infra
program_pace.ramp_summary: Contracts & golden sets → gateway & unit economics → orchestration & tools → retrieval → eval CI & policy → integrated platform → staff depth
program_pace.time_box_note: Skip optional videos unless you have a specific gap; every month ends in a prove artifact you can show in a design review.

0.title: Foundation week — first production habit
0.summary: Turn messy log-like text into typed records with retries and a golden set—the same contract mindset as bronze tables and GE tests.

where_it_applies.example: Application logs, webhook payloads, or CSV-adjacent text that is not yet in your warehouse schema.
where_it_applies.you_build: A small Python package: `extract(raw) -> Model`, pytest on fixtures, README metric.

where_it_applies.example: Before promoting a new parser in Spark/Glue, shadow-score 50 rows with the same contract.
where_it_applies.you_build: `data/golden/` + `scripts/score.py` run locally and in CI.

practice_ladder.name: Shadow
practice_ladder.action: Run extraction on synthetic/public samples only—no prod credentials.

practice_ladder.name: Harden

practice_ladder.exit: Forced provider failure switches model once; logged.

practice_ladder.name: Prove
practice_ladder.action: Public repo + pytest + prove checklist in course overview.
practice_ladder.exit: Reviewer runs commands in README in under 10 minutes.

1.title: Month 1 — LLM foundations where data platforms live
1.summary: Course 1 is not “learn AI from zero.” It gives you interview-grade mental models plus a gateway layer so any LLM step in your stack has cost, latency, and model attribution—like query tags on Snowflake or per-job DPU metrics on Glue.

where_it_applies.example: Vendor emails, support tickets, PDF tables, or API error blobs that today land as raw strings in S3 or VARIANT columns.
where_it_applies.you_build: Versioned `extract()` with low temperature, schema validation, and a golden set sampled from production-shaped fixtures (synthetic only in OSS).

where_it_applies.example: You add an LLM summarization or classification step next to dbt, Glue, or an ECS job.
where_it_applies.you_build: LiteLLM router/proxy; per-request log: model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, USD estimate.

where_it_applies.example: MWAA task logs, Glue stderr, or stack traces that engineers read manually today.
where_it_applies.you_build: CLI that outputs a **structured** triage object (severity, suspected layer, suggested checks)—human reviews before action.

where_it_applies.example: New Kafka topic or landing JSON with evolving keys—before you lock Avro/Protobuf or Iceberg schema.
where_it_applies.you_build: Propose a Pydantic model from N sample events; DE reviews and commits schema—not auto-deploy.
skills_from_course: separate schema validity vs semantic correctness

where_it_applies.example: Great Expectations or custom DQ failure with context rows—stakeholders want a paragraph, not a stack trace.
where_it_applies.you_build: Narration step that must cite input fields; validate shape; never auto-delete data.

where_it_applies.example: Cube YAML, dbt model descriptions, or Glue column comments that drift from reality.
where_it_applies.you_build: Batch job: table metadata in → suggested dimension/measure descriptions out → human PR to semantic repo.

practice_ladder.name: Mental model (time-boxed)
practice_ladder.action: Karpathy intro + one Applied LLMs section; write half a page: tokens, context limit, one failure mode.
practice_ladder.exit: You can explain LLM limits to your team without hand-waving.

practice_ladder.name: Shadow CLI on fixtures
practice_ladder.action: Extend boot repo: `your-cli extract --sample data/golden/001.json` with logging fields above.
practice_ladder.exit: Ten golden rows pass; failures are explicit validation errors.

practice_ladder.name: Gateway in the path
practice_ladder.action: All model calls go through LiteLLM; document primary + fallback models in README.
practice_ladder.exit: Table row per request in README or exported JSONL sample.

practice_ladder.name: Release prove
practice_ladder.action: Tag `v0.2`; paste release URL in studio Lab & Prove.

1.week_at_work: Pick **one** scenario above that matches work you understand (reconciliation, DQ, or landing parsing). Use **only** synthetic or public data in the OSS repo; pilot internally only with written approval and a gateway.
1.maps_to_prove: v0.2 release prove — LiteLLM router + README cost/latency/token table
anti_patterns: Sending production PII to a public API without legal/security sign-off
Replacing GE/dbt tests with an LLM “it looks fine”
Watching entire 16h playlists when the syllabus names one module
Skipping the metrics table—platform engineers are judged on unit economics

2.title: Month 2 — Orchestration like Airflow with state
2.summary: Wrap extraction in a graph: retries, checkpoints, and human approval when validation fails—same reliability patterns as saga workflows or MWAA sensors.

where_it_applies.example: Extract → validate → match → escalate when confidence low.
where_it_applies.you_build: LangGraph with `interrupt()` on fail path and documented resume steps.

practice_ladder.name: Linear graph
practice_ladder.action: Three nodes: ingest, extract, persist.
practice_ladder.exit: Single command runs end-to-end on golden sample.

practice_ladder.name: HITL branch
practice_ladder.action: On validation error, interrupt and require human JSON fix.
practice_ladder.exit: README demo of fail → fix → resume.

2.week_at_work: Model one real pipeline stage that already has a manual approval (e.g. finance sign-off) as a graph node.
